clue.text: Knowing when to find time in day

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: in tells us the time letter goes inside the shortened day name

parts.note: Tue is the short form of Tuesday

explanation.surface: Someone shrewd knows which slot in the day to set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a shrewd, perceptive person is described as knowing.

clue.text: Manic bee spoiled atmosphere

indicators.note: spoiled says the letters of manic bee are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A frantic bee has ruined the mood of a garden party.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the mood or feel of a place is its atmosphere.

clue.text: American argued after public transport crushed

indicators.note: after puts the argued word behind the transport

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport
pled is the American past tense of plead, to argue a case

explanation.surface: A US passenger argues after being squashed on a crowded tram.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something trodden underfoot has been crushed.

clue.text: Cheap time in New York

explanation.surface: A budget stay in Manhattan.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tinny describes cheap, flimsy goods made of thin metal.

clue.text: Kind and discerning? Me too!

parts.note: like as a noun means sort or kind, as in 'the like of it'
wise means discerning or sensible

explanation.surface: A compliment is returned: you are kind and perceptive, and so am I.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: saying 'in the same way' in reply is a way of agreeing that the same holds for oneself.

clue.text: One who knows the secrets of popular drink we hear

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: we hear says the drink is heard, not spelt

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: A connoisseur who knows the secrets of a fashionable tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone within an organisation, privy to its confidential information.

clue.text: Priest swimming in river shows proficiency

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled letters inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England

indicators.note: swimming says the letters of priest move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A cleric taking a dip in the river proves he can swim well.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: expertise is skill or know-how.

clue.text: Spoil naughty child's appearance

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
air means appearance or manner, as in 'an air of calm'

explanation.surface: A cheeky child's looks are ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to damage or weaken something is to spoil it.

clue.text: Infuriate general left out in action

indicators.note: in action says the remaining letters are set moving into a new order
out says the left letter is dropped from general

explanation.surface: A general is made furious when left out of the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L from GENERAL, leaving GENERA, which 'in action' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make someone very angry is to infuriate them.

clue.text: Break alcove

definitions.meaning: a pause in proceedings, such as parliament's holiday
a nook set back into a wall

explanation.surface: A short break in a nook.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adjournment or interval, and a niche set into a wall.

clue.text: Idiotic having no support around home

indicators.note: around says the support-free word wraps round the home word

parts.note: going without a bra, the garment of support, is braless
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone foolish leaves home without any support.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lacking a brain, that is any intelligence, means stupid or foolish.

clue.text: Primate in spin daily?

indicators.note: in puts the primate inside the spin abbreviation

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the trade of putting spin on stories
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey appears in a slanted story in the morning newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a daily is a newspaper published every day, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Starts to employ mindfulness practising tantric yoga bare

indicators.note: starts to says take the opening letter of each of the next five words

explanation.surface: Advice to begin practising mindfulness while doing tantric yoga with nothing on.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bare room or shelf has nothing in it, so is vacant.

clue.text: Signing off on finale involving yellow submarine to start with

indicators.note: involving says the finale word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: an ending is a finale
or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow

indicators.note: to start with picks out the opening letter of submarine

explanation.surface: A nod to the Beatles' song Yellow Submarine as the closing number.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: signing off on a cheque or plan means approving or countersigning it.

clue.text: Drives heartless copper to church on Sabbath

indicators.note: heartless says the middle letters of copper are taken away

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
S is short for Sabbath or Sunday

explanation.surface: An unfeeling policeman drives off to church on Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes PP, the centre of copper, leaving COER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to drive someone to do something is to force or pressure them.

clue.text: Admitted deploying seconds to collect iron

indicators.note: to collect says the shuffled letters take the iron symbol inside
deploying says the letters of seconds are spread out into a new arrangement

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A soldier owned up to sending backup troops to fetch metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have owned up to something is to have admitted it.

clue.text: Attack Republican disaster-relief funding

parts.note: aid is money or supplies sent after a disaster

explanation.surface: A politician assails the government's spending on disaster relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a raid is a sudden assault or strike.

clue.text: Reveal chap providing electric shock treatment

parts.note: a chap is a man
if means providing or on condition that
EST is electroshock therapy

explanation.surface: A man discloses that he will give electric shock treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make plain or show clearly is to reveal.

clue.text: Disheartened daughter gets expelled

parts.note: to be ejected is to be thrown out or expelled

explanation.surface: A daughter is downcast after being thrown out of school.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dispirited and low in spirits.

clue.text: Animals celebrated revolution

indicators.note: revolution turns the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: to celebrate someone in song is to have sung of them

explanation.surface: Creatures that cheered an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: wildebeest, these African antelopes, are animals.

clue.text: Clean steps surrounding queen

indicators.note: surrounding says the steps word goes round the queen

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: Royal staff scrub the stairs around the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sterile means free of germs, perfectly hygienic.

clue.text: Cow on top of a headless sheep

parts.note: over means above or on top of

indicators.note: headless says the first letter of the sheep word is dropped

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A cow sits on top of a sheep with no head: a grisly farmyard scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to cow someone is to intimidate or daunt them.

clue.text: Slow broadband provider carrying nothing to exploit

indicators.note: carrying says the provider bears the nothing letter at its front

parts.note: O is the zero digit, nothing
BT is British Telecom, a UK broadband company
to use someone is to exploit them

explanation.surface: A sluggish internet company carries nothing worth using.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: slow in the sense of dim-witted, slow to understand.

clue.text: Beers oddly containing bone and carrots

indicators.note: containing says the odd letters hold the bone inside
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of beers

parts.note: a rib is a bone

explanation.surface: A pub menu: beer served with a rib bone and some vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a carrot in the sense of 'carrot and stick' is an inducement, so carrots are inducements.

clue.text: Join Labour leader in excitement

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the excitement word

parts.note: spice means zest or excitement

indicators.note: leader picks out the opening letter of labour

explanation.surface: An invitation to sign up with the Labour Party leader in a fervour.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to splice is to join two ends together, as with rope or film.

clue.text: Show on here

parts.note: re means on or concerning
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: A curt announcement that a performance is on here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to show or depict something in a picture is to portray it.

clue.text: Arrest witnesses reported

indicators.note: reported says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to witness something is to see it, so witnesses means sees

explanation.surface: A news item about an arrest that bystanders saw.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to arrest a person or goods is to take hold of them by force.

clue.text: Drunken bout regularly superseded

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of superseded, starting from the first

explanation.surface: A binge that has been routinely replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a spree is a session of heavy drinking or wild indulgence.

clue.text: Receding fossil beds uncovered paradise

indicators.note: Receding says the hidden letters are read backwards
uncovered says letters are dug out of the words fossil beds

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Eroding rock strata reveal fossils: heaven for a palaeontologist.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read 'uncovered paradise' as the definition, but 'uncovered' is the hiding signal, like fossils exposed in rock, and 'paradise' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: perfect happiness is often called heaven or paradise.

clue.text: Rising to almost cover courteous male

indicators.note: almost says the final letter of the cover word is cut off

parts.note: to insure something is to provide cover for it
a gent is a courteous, gentlemanly man

explanation.surface: A polite man is climbing up so he can nearly provide cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: rebels rising in revolt against authority are in insurrection.

clue.text: Balanced meal in irregularly sided container

indicators.note: in places the meal inside the shuffled letters
irregularly says the letters of sided are put in a new order

parts.note: tea is a light evening meal in Britain

explanation.surface: A packed meal sits steady in a lopsided lunchbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'container' is surface colour for the box; the word 'in' is the instruction that places the meal inside the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something steadied has been made stable, kept in equilibrium.

clue.text: Hired journalist following split

indicators.note: following puts the journalist after the split word

parts.note: rent means torn apart or split
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter taken on after a falling-out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a car or flat that has been hired is one paid for to use.
